blocks.text: CSS Lists
CSS Styling Lists
In HTML, there are two main types of lists:

items: <ul> - unordered lists (list items are marked with bullets)
<ol> - ordered lists (list items are marked with numbers or letters)

blocks.text: CSS has the following properties for styling HTML lists:

items:
list-style-type
  - Specifies the type of list-item marker

list-style-image
  - Specifies an image as the list-item marker

list-style-position
  - Specifies the position of the list-item markers

list-style
  - A shorthand property for the properties above

CSS Replace List-item Marker with an Image
The CSS list-style-image property is used to replace the list-item marker with an image.
Note: Always specify a list-style-type property in addition. This property is used if the image for some reason is unavailable.

blocks.text: CSS Position the List-item Markers

The CSS list-style-position
  property specifies the position of the list-item markers
(bullet points).

list-style-position: outside; means that the bullet points will be outside
the list item. The start of each line of a list item will be aligned vertically.
This is default:

list-style-position: inside; means that the bullet points will be inside
the list item. As it is part of the list item, it will be part of the text and
push the text at the start:
